concepts.definition: Mechanical contacts chattering for a short time as they close, making the pin go back and forth between HIGH and LOW several times.
concepts.example: You press a real button once, and the counter goes up by 3 instead of 1.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking debouncing is unnecessary because the lab button does not bounce.

concepts.definition: In debouncing, the time a pin value must stay unchanged before it is accepted (for example 20 ms).
concepts.example: If the pin is still LOW 20 ms after the last change, the press is accepted.
concepts.pitfall: Choosing the time too short lets bounce leak through; choosing it too long misses fast presses.

concepts.definition: The time between an event happening and the program responding to it.
concepts.example: If there is a delay(500) inside loop, the button response can be up to 500 ms late.
concepts.pitfall: Making another job wait with delay and expecting the button to be listened to during the same time.

concepts.definition: The slow job keeping its own time with millis(), while the other inputs are read on every pass inside loop().
concepts.example: "tik" is printed every 500 ms, but the button is checked on every pass.
concepts.pitfall: Printing a message on every pass while the button is held and filling the Serial monitor; edge detection is needed.

quiz.prompt: Why does a counter that does not prevent bounce make several counts on a single press of a real button?
options: During the press the pin goes back and forth between HIGH and LOW for a short time, and every change to LOW is counted
The Arduino is designed to read the button twice
INPUT_PULLUP connects both ends of the button to 5 V
Because the counter is an int, it doubles the number
quiz.explanation: Because the contacts hit each other and chatter, the pin changes several times on a single press, and code that detects edges counts every falling edge. The Arduino does not read the button twice; INPUT_PULLUP pulls the pin up to 5 V, not the button's pin; an int does not multiply the number of counts.

quiz.prompt: In the debounce code, SAKIN_SURE = 20 ms. For a press to be counted, for at least how many ms must the pin stay unchanged?
quiz.explanation: The code resets the time on every change and only accepts the value when it has stayed calm for 20 ms. That is why a press released before 20 ms are up is not counted; this is the cost of the waiting time.

options: It prints BASILDI all the time
quiz.explanation: After reading the pin, the program sleeps for 500 ms. Because the press starts and ends within the 500 ms between two readings, it is never seen. Unless a reading happens to fall exactly at the moment of the press, a short press is missed; if it were read on every pass with millis(), it would be caught.

options: It should be sayac-- instead of sayac++
analogRead should be used instead of digitalRead
In the if (ham != sonHam) block, sonDegisim = millis(); is missing
quiz.explanation: Because the time of the last change is never updated, millis() - sonDegisim always stays above 20; in practice there is no wait, and every bounce is accepted at once. In the correct code, the timer is reset every time the pin changes (sonDegisim = millis()). The other options do not fix the bug; making 20 into 0 removes the wait completely.

quiz.prompt: A program has a delay(50) inside loop(), and the pin is read only once per pass. For at least how many ms must you hold the button down to be sure it is caught?
quiz.explanation: The time between two readings is about 50 ms. A press shorter than this can fit between two readings and be missed; a press of 50 ms or longer falls on at least one reading. Reducing the delay to 5 or using millis() makes this gap smaller.
